tasks.gr11-soil-formation-erosion-t4: Topic: Soil Formation and Soil Erosion. Cover the five soil-forming factors (parent material, climate, organisms, topography, time), soil horizons (O, A, B, C, R profile), types of soil erosion (sheet, rill, gully, wind deflation), and conservation methods (contour ploughing, terracing, strip cropping, afforestation). Ask Grade 11 learners to describe a soil profile, explain the impact of overgrazing on erosion, or evaluate a soil conservation strategy.
tasks.gr11-energy-resources-t4: Topic: Conventional and Non-Conventional Energy Resources. Cover fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) and nuclear energy as conventional sources; solar, wind, hydroelectric, geothermal, and biomass as renewable alternatives; South Africa's energy mix and load-shedding challenge; and the REIPPPP (Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme). Ask Grade 11 learners to compare the advantages and disadvantages of two energy sources, explain South Africa's reliance on coal, or evaluate the role of renewables in energy security.
tasks.gr11-greener-economies-t4: Topic: Greener Economies and Sustainability. Cover the green economy concept, the circular economy, South Africa's carbon tax, the Paris Agreement and NDCs, green building practices, and how GIS supports sustainability planning and monitoring. Ask Grade 11 learners to define a green economy, explain the difference between a linear and circular economy, describe South Africa's climate commitments, or explain how GIS can monitor deforestation.
tasks.gr11-resource-sustainability-t4: Topic: Resource Use and Sustainability. Cover renewable vs non-renewable resources, overexploitation challenges (deforestation, groundwater depletion, overfishing), the ecological footprint concept, Earth Overshoot Day, and pathways to sustainability (conservation, recycling, green technology, community-based natural resource management). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate or interpret an ecological footprint, explain the consequences of overexploiting a named resource, or evaluate a community-based conservation strategy.
